# triage-demo

A repository that runs its tests on every pull request.

## Contributing

Open a pull request. Contributions arrive from forks.

input.content:
---
name: triage

on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened]

permissions: {}

jobs:
  triage:
    name: Welcome and label
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # No checkout step here: this job only needs the pull_request event
    # metadata (author, title, number), never the fork's code or scripts.
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
      issues: write
    steps:
      - name: Ensure needs-triage label exists
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          gh label create needs-triage \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --color ededed \
            --description "Needs maintainer triage" \
            --force

      - name: Post welcome comment
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          PR_AUTHOR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}
          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
        run: |
          gh pr comment "$PR_NUMBER" \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --body "Welcome, @${PR_AUTHOR}! Thanks for opening \"${PR_TITLE}\". A maintainer will triage this shortly."

      - name: Apply needs-triage label
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
        run: |
          gh pr edit "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$REPO" --add-label needs-triage

# triage-demo

A repository that runs its tests on every pull request.

## Contributing

Open a pull request. Contributions arrive from forks.

## Workflows

- **ci** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) — runs the test suite on every pull request.
- **triage** (`.github/workflows/triage.yml`) — runs when a pull request is opened, including from
  forks. It posts a welcome comment that mentions the contributor and the pull request title, and
  applies the `needs-triage` label. It uses the `pull_request_target` event to get permission to
  comment and label, but never checks out or executes the fork's code — it only reads pull request
  metadata (author, title, number) from the event payload.

content.text:
Added a triage workflow and README section. Summary:

**`.github/workflows/triage.yml`** — triggers on `pull_request_target` (`opened`), which works correctly for fork PRs since `pull_request` alone only grants a read-only token for forked contributions. Key safety property: it never checks out or runs any code from the fork — it only reads event metadata (`author`, `title`, `number`) and calls the GitHub API via `gh`. Values that could contain shell metacharacters (title, author) are passed through `env:` and referenced as `$VAR` inside `run:`, not interpolated directly via `${{ }}` in the script body, avoiding script-injection risk. Permissions are scoped to just `pull-requests: write` and `issues: write`. It creates the `needs-triage` label if missing (`--force`), posts the welcome comment, then applies the label.

Validated the YAML with `python3 -c "yaml.safe_load(...)"` and with `actionlint`, both clean.

**README.md** — added a "Workflows" section documenting both `ci` and `triage`, explaining the fork-safety rationale for `pull_request_target`.
